claim: 2-legged OAuth uses a JWT client assertion (RFC 7523 style) signed with the client secret using an HMAC-SHA algorithm, sent with grant_type=client_credentials and the X-AMEX-API-KEY header carrying the client_id.

note: Quote: "The Client Assertion is a JWT signed with the Client Secret (provided via the American Express Developers Portal) using any recommended HMAC SHA algorithm" · Required claims iss, sub, aud ([https://americanexpress.com]), exp, jti; client_assertion_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer; headers X-CorrelationID (UUID), X-AMEX-API-KEY ('This is a client_id value and will be provided via the American Express Developers Portal.'), Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded. The spec viewer supports four security models: oneWayTLS_AppKey, oAuth, oneWayTLS_HMAC, mTLS_HMAC (bundle). · fetch curl

claim: Legacy products (Amex Token Service, Enhanced Authorization v2) use an HMAC-SHA256 MAC Authorization header built from client ID, epoch-millisecond timestamp, nonce, body hash and signature, with the client secret as the key.

Catalogue types Amex Token Service and Enhanced Authorization v2 as LEGACY_HMAC. Java/.NET client-core repos implement HmacAuthProvider. · fetch curl

claim: The entire Mastercard Developers reference can be read logged out: every documentation URL serves a plain-markdown twin at /index.md, and a 527 KB llms.txt indexes 94 documented services.

claim: Sandbox credentials are self-service: sign up, create a project, select APIs, generate and download credentials, and test in Sandbox with no approval step for most APIs.
title: Quick Start Guide | Platform Overview | Mastercard Developers
note: Quote: "Click the “Open Project” button. Now you’re ready to test in Sandbox." · Rendered in a browser tab logged out; the same page is also served as quick-start-guide/index.md (7,105 bytes, fetched by curl). Steps: create/activate account, create project, select APIs, 'Generate and download your credentials', open project. Team Management doc adds: 'A project can have a maximum of 10 admin members and a maximum of 20 members in total.'

claim: Not every sandbox is open: some services put a new project's Sandbox access into an 'Under Review' state pending the service team's approval, and private services are hidden from the API picker until access is requested.
title: Quick Start Guide | Platform Overview | Mastercard Developers
note: Quote: "Some services require approval before granting access to their Sandbox environment." · Same FAQ also says: 'A service may not appear in the APIs dropdown if it’s private and you don’t have access to it.' A forum post of 2026-08-31 shows a Confirmed Fraud (FLD) project stuck at 'SANDBOX Pending'.

claim: Portal-issued keys expire after 13 months; the portal emails expiry reminders, although the two docs disagree on the reminder schedule.
title: Quick Start Guide | Platform Overview | Mastercard Developers
note: Quote: "Keys generated on Mastercard Developers are valid for 13 months." · Quick Start says reminders at '60, 30, 15, 5, and 1 day'; the OAuth Keys guide says '90, 60, 30, 15, 7, and 1 day(s)'. See contradictions.

claim: Production credentials are minted instantly at request time but stay inactive until Mastercard approves the production request; prerequisites are company verification, 'commercial countries' and a Business Relationship Type that covers the API.
title: Quick Start Guide | Platform Overview | Mastercard Developers
note: Quote: "Production credentials are generated instantaneously but they are only activated once your Production request is approved." · BRT doc (account-management/business-relationship-type/index.md): 'To request Production access, the API services added to your project must align with the BRT assigned to your company.' Missing BRTs are added via an emailed 'Customer Onboarding Platform' questionnaire; 'It may take up to 2 hours' to reflect. SSO customers skip company verification.

claim: Company verification on the developer portal is keyed to the Mastercard Company ID (CID) and pre-populates from the company's Mastercard Connect account, tying the developer portal to the gated client portal.
title: Company Verification
note: Quote: "If a corresponding Mastercard Connect account is found, the company data will be pre-populated." · CID is 'a 6-10 digit ID that Mastercard assigns to a business'. Verified accounts show a VERIFIED badge on My Account. Non-Connect customers enter company details and a request goes for manual review ('VERIFICATION IN PROGRESS'). · fetch curl

claim: OAuth 1.0a with RSA-SHA256 request signing is the default authentication scheme across the portal; OAuth 2.0 (FAPI 2.0) and mutual TLS are the two alternatives.
title: Authentication
note: Quote: "This is the default authentication mechanism used by most APIs on Mastercard Developers." · Page lists three protocols: OAuth 1.0a, OAuth 2.0 ('client credentials flow' plus FAPI 2.0), Mutual TLS (mTLS). No plain API-key scheme is offered. · fetch curl

claim: OAuth 1.0a mechanics: a 97-character non-secret consumer key plus a 2048-bit RSA private signing key (RSA only), signature method fixed to RSA-SHA256 with the oauth_body_hash extension; the portal can generate the key pair in the browser so Mastercard never holds the private key.
title: Using OAuth 1.0a to Access Mastercard APIs
note: Quote: "Consumer keys are 97-character identifiers for client applications consuming Mastercard APIs." · 'The signing key is a 2048-bit private RSA key'; 'It must be RSA-SHA256'. CSR doc: 'For OAuth 1.0a, only RSA keys are supported'. OAuth Keys guide: 'When you choose this option, your browser generates the private key and downloads it for you. Mastercard never sees your private key.' Keys are delivered as PKCS#12 (.p12). · fetch curl

claim: Mastercard's OAuth 2.0 is the FAPI 2.0 Security Profile: client authentication by private_key_jwt and sender-constrained access tokens via DPoP (ES256 or PS256), with a DPoP-Nonce handshake; sandbox token endpoint is sandbox.api.mastercard.com/oauth/token and example tokens live 900 seconds.
title: Using OAuth 2.0 to Access Mastercard APIs
note: Quote: "Mastercard implements the "FAPI2SP private key + DPoP" approach, which creates 2 layers of protection:" · Guide shows htu 'https://sandbox.api.mastercard.com/oauth/token' and a token response with '"expires_in": 900'. Only the sandbox token endpoint is printed; no production token URL found. OAuth Keys guide: 'For OAuth 2.0 keys, there is no rotate option. Instead, you add a new key and switch to it before the old one expires.' · fetch curl

claim: Auth scheme by service, as tagged in llms.txt: 73 services OAuth1.0a only, 7 OAuth1.0a and OAuth2 (FAPI 2.0), 5 MTLS, 5 NONE (documentation-only), 4 OpenBanking, out of 94 serviceId entries.

claim: Sensitive fields are protected by an application-layer encryption scheme in addition to TLS: JWE compact serialization (RSA-OAEP, AES-CBC or AES-GCM) for field-level or whole-payload encryption, plus a legacy 'Mastercard encryption' format; open-source client-encryption libraries implement both.
title: Securing Sensitive Data Using Payload Encryption
note: Quote: "Mastercard uses JWE compact serialization for the encryption of sensitive data and supports both field level encryption and entire payload encryption." · Link markup stripped from quote. Legacy scheme 'involves an initialization vector, an encrypted or wrapped key, an encrypted value, a public key fingerprint and a digest algorithm' with RSA-OAEP SHA256/SHA512. Encryption certificates are issued per project via Credential Management. · fetch curl

claim: Mastercard Connect, the client portal that the developer docs point to for the Key Management Portal and Support Case Management, is a hard login wall requiring a User ID plus password or RSA SecurID token.
title: Mastercard Connect
note: Quote: "Sign in User ID Password / RSA SecurID® token" · Rendered in a browser tab; whitespace collapsed. curl: HTTP 302 to /mccsignin/users/auth-actions?heracles_operation=AUTHORIZATION... then 401. Page tagline: 'Where you connect with Mastercard to grow your business'; offers 'Sign up' and 'Replace RSA SecurID token'. Wall only documented; no login attempted.

claim: Participation is gated: an entity must be approved as a Customer, execute the applicable Licenses and pay associated fees before conducting any Activity (Rule 1.1).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 1.1 Eligibility to be a Customer, BIN Sponsor, or Affiliate Sponsoring Customer, PDF p.34
note: Quote: "no entity may participate in Activity until that entity is approved to be a Customer by the Corporation, has executed the applicable Licenses" · PDF (503 pages, 1.8 MB) fetched inside the browser pane session from the public Rules page and text-extracted with pdf.js; curl and WebFetch receive Akamai 403. Rule 1.5 adds that pending approval Mastercard 'may authorize the applicant to participate in Activity on an interim basis' at the applicant's own risk (p.41).

claim: To be a Principal or Affiliate an applicant must be a regulated financial institution (or other legal entity authorized for financial transactions) with acceptable business plans; admission is at Mastercard's sole discretion (Rule 1.1.1).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 1.1.1 Principal or Affiliate, PDF p.34
note: Quote: "A financial institution applicant must be regulated and supervised by one or more governmental authorities or agencies" · Same page: 'The decision to admit an applicant as a Principal or Affiliate of the Corporation is made at the sole discretion of the Corporation.' Non-FI applicants 'must satisfy such eligibility criteria as the Corporation may adopt from time to time'.

claim: An Affiliate Sponsoring Customer is a participation type for entities that sponsor Affiliates but cannot themselves issue or acquire; an Association is one form of it (Rules 1.1.2 and 1.1.3).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 1.1.3 Affiliate Sponsoring Customer, PDF p.35
note: Quote: "An Affiliate Sponsoring Customer does not have the regulatory authority to issue Cards or acquire Transactions itself" · Rule 1.1.2 (p.35): 'An Association is a type of Affiliate Sponsoring Customer.' Eligibility requires demonstrated ability 'to act as an operational hub for Affiliates'.

claim: Since 20 May 2025 a Principal must obtain Mastercard's approval before acting as BIN Sponsor for a Sponsored Program Manager (fintech/program-manager model), and that approval is revocable without notice (Rule 1.1.4).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 1.1.4 BIN Sponsor, PDF p.35
note: Quote: "Before becoming a BIN Sponsor for a Sponsored Program Manager, a Principal must obtain approval for such Activity from the Corporation." · 'This requirement applies with respect to all new and renewed Sponsored Program Manager registrations effected on or after 20 May 2025.'

claim: Payment Transfer Activity (money movement) has its own participation type, the PTA Customer, requiring approval, a PTA Agreement per program, and ISO/IEC 27001 or PCI DSS compliance (Rule 1.1.6).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 1.1.6 Payment Transfer Activity Customer, PDF p.36
note: Quote: "No entity may Participate in a PTA Program as a PTA Customer until that entity is approved to be a PTA Customer" · Eligibility list item 1 requires 'ISO/IEC 27001 or the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS)'. An entity 'may be a Principal for Payment Transfer Activity and an Affiliate for another Activity, or vice versa'.

claim: Digital Activity Customer is a non-issuing, non-acquiring participation type (wallets, token requestors) whose eligibility includes passing Mastercard certification and testing (Chapter 9, Rule 1.1.5).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Chapter 9 Digital Activity, Rule 1.1.5 Digital Activity Customer, PDF p.211
note: Quote: "The successful completion of such certification and testing procedures as the Corporation may require." · Definitions (p.472): a Digital Activity Customer 'may not issue Cards, acquire Transactions, or Sponsor any other Customer into the Corporation.' Rule 1.8 (p.212): each must sign a Digital Activity Agreement containing 'a limited License ... with no specified Area of Use'.

claim: Customers must meet minimum financial requirements set by Mastercard, which may include capital adequacy and subjective management assessments, and Mastercard may require collateral or escrow as a condition of participation (Rules 1.3 and 1.4).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 1.3 Satisfaction of Minimum Financial Requirements, PDF p.40
note: Quote: "Each Customer at all times must satisfy the minimum financial requirements established by the Corporation from time to time." · The actual thresholds are not published in the Rules. Rule 1.4 (p.41): participation may be conditioned on 'the establishment of escrow arrangements, the delivery of letters of credit'.

claim: AML and sanctions compliance programs are an explicit condition of being granted a License, and each Customer must keep AML and Sanctions Compliance contacts current in My Company Manager on Mastercard Connect (Rule 1.2).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 1.2 Mastercard Anti-Money Laundering and Sanctions Requirements, PDF p.36-37
note: Quote: "As a condition of being granted a License and/or as a condition of an execution of a PTA Agreement by the Corporation" · p.37: contacts must be provided 'in the My Company Manager application on Mastercard Connect'. Failure 'may result in: The denial of a License'.

claim: Mastercard alone decides the level of participation (Principal vs Affiliate) for each applicant, Customer, Service Provider and Network Enablement Partner; a Customer's License is limited to an Area of Use (Rules 1.9 and 1.7).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 1.9 Participation in Activity(ies) and Digital Activity, PDF p.46
note: Quote: "The Corporation has the right to determine the appropriate level of Participation (for example, Affiliate or Principal) for each applicant" · Rule 1.7 (p.42): 'each Customer may use a Mark and conduct Activity solely in the Area of Use in which the Customer has been granted a License'; 1.7.1 requires an application to extend it. Rule 1.9.3 (p.47): 'An Affiliate cannot Sponsor another Affiliate'.

claim: Under the sponsor model the Principal or Affiliate Sponsoring Customer is liable to Mastercard and all other Customers for everything its Sponsored Affiliates, Sponsored Program Managers and Co-brand Partners do (Rule 2.2.2).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 2.2.2 Obligations of a Sponsor, PDF p.65
note: Quote: "Each Sponsor is liable to the Corporation and to all other Customers for all Activities of each of its Sponsored Affiliates"

claim: The Rules define a Principal as a Customer that participates directly using its own BINs/IINs and may sponsor Affiliates; 'Participation' is Mastercard's term for membership, and a Customer may be a Principal, Association, Affiliate, Digital Activity Customer, Sponsored Digital Activity Entity or PTA Customer.
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Definitions: Principal (PDF p.491), Customer (p.471), Participation
note: Quote: "A Customer that participates directly in Activity using its assigned BINs/IINs and that may Sponsor one or more Affiliates." · Definitions: 'For a Mastercard Customer, Participation is an alternative term for Membership.' and 'A Customer may be a Principal, Association, Affiliate, Digital Activity Customer, Sponsored Digital Activity Entity, or PTA Customer.'

claim: Each Customer is identified by an ICA number assigned by Mastercard; ICA and BIN assignment are part of onboarding and, for API products, are set up with the regional customer representative.
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Definitions: ICA
note: Quote: "A unique number assigned by the Corporation to identify a Customer in relation to Activity." · Mastercard Send docs add: 'An Interbank Card Association (ICA) number is a unique identification number assigned by Mastercard to identify each OI and TI.'

claim: In the US Region a Mastercard Affiliate may participate indirectly through a Type I TPP's ICAs and BINs (a processor can sponsor an issuing Affiliate), but must be sponsored by a Principal or Association for acquiring.
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Chapter 16 United States Region, Definitions: Mastercard Affiliate, PDF p.355; Rule 7.9 Type I TPP Obligations, p.369
note: Quote: "participates indirectly in Mastercard Activity through the Sponsorship of a Mastercard Principal, an Association, or a Type I TPP" · US Rule 7.9: 'a Type I TPP in the U.S. Region may Sponsor an Affiliate to engage in Mastercard and/or Maestro issuing Activity' and may participate in Settlement as agent. US definitions also name a 'debit Licensee' with a License 'limited to the issuance of Debit Mastercard Cards' (Rule 8.6, p.371).

claim: Third parties are categorized as Service Providers by program service (3-DSSP, AML/Sanctions SP, BPSP, DSE, DASP, DCC SP, ISO, Installment SP, MMSP, Staged DWO, TSP, Payment Facilitator, Merchant Payment Gateway, Terminal Servicer, Co-brand Partner, Sponsored Program Manager, BIN Sponsor Partner, TPP) and may only perform the service they are registered for (Rule 7.1).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Chapter 7 Service Providers and Network Enablement Partners, Rule 7.1 Service Provider Categories and Descriptions, PDF p.155-165
note: Quote: "A Service Provider may only perform the Program Services such Service Provider is registered by the Customer to perform." · ISO Program Service includes 'Terminal deployment, not including ATM Terminal deployment by an ATM Terminal owner that does not perform any other type of ISO Program Service' (p.158), so a pure ATM deployer is not an ISO. A corporate affiliate serving only its parent Customer 'is deemed not to be a Service Provider' (p.155).

claim: Mastercard stopped designating new Type I TPPs on 20 May 2025; existing Type I TPPs may remain, and Type I registration is no longer available in Europe.
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 7.1 TPP subcategories, PDF p.165; Rule 7.10.2, p.189
note: Quote: "As of 20 May 2025, Service Providers are no longer designated as Type I TPPs." · p.189: 'Registration as a Type I TPP is no longer available in the Europe Region. Any existing Type I TPP may remain a Type I TPP.' Type II is any TPP not deemed Type I; Type III is a US Region category.

claim: Service Provider registration is done by the sponsoring Customer (not the third party) through the My Company Manager application on Mastercard Connect, with required materials due within 30 days and an annual re-validation (Rule 7.10).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 7.10 Registration and Validation Requirements for Service Providers, PDF p.186-188
note: Quote: "provide all information and material required by the Corporation in connection with the proposed registration to the My Company Manager application or service_provider@mastercard.com" · Customer must also 'Validate that the Customer understands, meets and validates the Customer's responsibilities ... within 30 days of the registration application submission date and once during each calendar year thereafter.' Rule 7.10.7 (p.190): failure is 'subject to noncompliance assessments of up to USD 25,000 for each 30-day period of noncompliance.' A Service Provider must be registered separately by each Customer and for each Program Service (items 5 and 6, p.187).

claim: Registration carries an initial fee and an annual renewal fee billed to the Customer via MCBS (or directly to a Type I/Type III TPP); the amounts are not published in the Rules, which point to the Pricing and Billing Center on Mastercard Connect.
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 7.10 item 3, PDF p.187; Rule 3.8 Fees, Assessments, and Other Payment Obligations, p.76
note: Quote: "an initial registration fee and the applicable annual renewal fee is charged by the Corporation to the Customer and debited from the Customer using MCBS" · Rule 3.8: fees are those 'including those set forth in the Pricing and Billing Center on Mastercard Connect'. US Rule 7.10.3 (p.371): for Type III TPPs 'the applicable fee is charged by the Corporation directly to the Type III TPP.' No public fee schedule for licensing or registration was found.

claim: A Service Provider that touches cardholder data must validate PCI compliance under the Site Data Protection program (via pcireports@mastercard.com) before registration is complete, and the Customer must receive written confirmation before using the provider.
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 7.10 item 1-2, PDF p.187
note: Quote: "The registration of a proposed Service Provider will not be deemed complete until the Customer's compliance is validated." · 'The Customer must receive the Corporation's written confirmation of the registration before using a Service Provider for Program Service.' A compliance action plan may be accepted for non-compliant providers 'except that a compliance plan is not acceptable for Type I TPP Service Providers.'

claim: A TPP designated Type I must register within 90 days using TPP Registration Form 919 plus an SSAE 18 or ISAE 3402 audit report and a business continuity form, emailed to tpp_registration@mastercard.com (Rule 7.10.2).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 7.10.2 Registration Requirements for Type I TPPs, PDF p.188
note: Quote: "the TPP must submit TPP Registration Form 919 SSAE 18 or ISAE 3402 (or a Corporation approved equivalent standard) form and business continuity form" · Type I TPPs must inform Mastercard 'of all ICA numbers pertaining to which such Type I TPP is performing any Program Service' (p.189).

claim: Network Enablement Partner (NEP) is a direct-contract tier for operationally significant Service Providers: a provider may apply, or Mastercard may designate it, after which it must sign an NEP Agreement within 30 days or Customers must stop using it within 180 days (Rules 7.11.1-7.11.2).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 7.11 Network Enablement Partners, PDF p.190-195
note: Quote: "May be designated by the Corporation to be a Network Enablement Partner, when deemed by the Corporation to be operationally significant" · Applicants 'complete and submit the NEP Application form to service_provider@mastercard.com'. NEPs pay their own 'registration and renewal fees' (7.11.3 item 6), are bound by Rules 2.2.7, 2.3, 2.4, 2.5, 3.7, 3.8, 3.15 and AML/sanctions 'as if such Network Enablement Partner was a Customer', are jointly and severally liable with registering Customers (7.11.4.4), and 'may apply to the Corporation to participate in the testing of assets of the Corporation (for example, an ICA or a BIN)' (7.11.4.5).

claim: Certain roles must be NEPs: a Payment Facilitator submitting direct to the Interchange System where its Acquirer cannot see transactions, a Payment Facilitator of Specialty Merchants, and any BIN Sponsor Partner.
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 7.8.2 item 8 and 7.8.3, PDF p.186; Rule 7.7.7 BIN Sponsor Partner, p.180
note: Quote: "whose Acquirer does not have the ability to see such Transactions at the time of submission, must register as a Network Enablement Partner." · Rule 7.7.7: 'The BIN Sponsor Partner must be approved by the Corporation as a Network Enablement Partner with permission to act as a BIN Sponsor Partner.' Rule 7.7.6 (p.179): 'Only one Sponsored Program Manager is permitted per Card Program' and an SPM 'Becomes a Network Enablement Partner, when specified by the Standards'.

claim: A Token Service Provider must complete Mastercard's certification and testing procedures before a Customer may register it; Customers must also verify any Service Provider is a bona fide business with adequate data safeguards (Rule 7.2).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 7.2 The Performance of Program Service, PDF p.165
note: Quote: "Prior to registering a TSP, confirm that such entity satisfies all certification and testing procedures established by the Corporation" · The certification procedures themselves are not described in the public Rules.

claim: The Rules' own audience metadata names the partner roles Mastercard documents for, including Branded Processor, Network Enablement Partner, MPGS (gateway) resellers and merchants, and a 'Global Vendor Certification Program' for vendors.
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), front matter Table 1 Details (Audience), PDF p.24
note: Quote: "Acquirer, Branded Processor, Issuer, Network Enablement Partner, MPGS Acquirer Reseller, MPGS Merchant, MPGS Non-Acquirer Reseller, Processor, Vendor - Global Vendor Certification Program" · Same page directs non-urgent questions to 'Create a case on the Technical Resource Center to create a case in Support Case Management' and urgent ones to Customer Technical Services by phone. No public page describing the Global Vendor Certification Program was found.

claim: A senior executive of each Principal, Affiliate Sponsoring Customer, Affiliate, NEP and Digital Activity Customer must certify compliance with any Standard in writing on request (Rule 2.1.5), the only 'certification' rule in Chapter 2.
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 2.1.5 Certification, PDF p.62
note: Quote: "A senior executive officer of each Principal, Affiliate Sponsoring Customer, Affiliate, Network Enablement Partner, and Digital Activity Customer must, if requested by the Corporation" · Customers must also take part 'in mandatory training designed to ensure the Customer understands its responsibilities under the Standards' (Rule 2.2.1 item 10, p.65).

claim: Customers may join other ATM networks as issuer or acquirer alongside the Mastercard ATM Network provided they are not Competing ATM Networks (Rule 1.10), and acquirers of ATM owners must run their own ATM AML monitoring (Rule 1.2.1.1).
title: Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026 edition), Rule 1.10 Participation in Competing Networks, PDF p.47; Rule 1.2.1.1, p.39
note: Quote: "A Customer may take part, as either an issuer or an acquirer or both, in any ATM network in addition to the Mastercard" · p.39: 'the Acquirer of any ATM Owners or Service Providers who process ATM Transactions are obligated to monitor ATM Activity regardless of the monitoring obligation of the Issuer.' Rule 5.1.3 sets required ATM Owner Agreement terms (p.108).

claim: For EEA/UK/Gibraltar switching, a Network Participant must test and obtain certification of its equipment and connections before switching, and must file routing tables (IRT/IDF) at least five business days before going live (Switch Rules 4.1-4.2).
title: Mastercard Switch Rules (16 December 2025), Chapter 4 Connecting to the Network and Authorization Routing, PDF p.43
note: Quote: "the Network Participant must perform testing and obtain any necessary certifications of its equipment, procedures, and Network connections as may be required" · PDF (114 pages) fetched inside the browser pane and text-extracted with pdf.js. p.11: applies to 'intra-EEA/United Kingdom/Gibraltar Transactions'; a Network Participant 'indicates its agreement to respect these rules in writing and/or by the act of using the Network'. Routing: 'no later than five business days prior to the requested effective date of live switching'.

claim: Mastercard Developers is self-service to Sandbox: sign up, create a project, download credentials and test; Production credentials are issued instantly but only activate after Mastercard reviews and approves the Production request.
title: Quick Start Guide | Mastercard Developers
note: Quote: "Production credentials are generated instantaneously but they are only activated once your Production request is approved." · Page is a JS app; text read in the browser pane (curl returns the shell only; the same content is served as markdown at /platform/documentation/quick-start-guide/index.md). claim: X-Pay Token is an HMAC-SHA256 signature scheme: the apikey travels as a query parameter and the x-pay-token header is 'xv2:' + UTC timestamp + ':' + HMAC over timestamp, resource path, query string and body.

claim: Message Level Encryption on VDP is JWE-based: payloads are AES-GCM encrypted (128- or 256-bit) with the content key wrapped by RSA-OAEP 2048, using separate Visa (request) and client (response) key pairs identified by a Key-ID header.

note: Quote: "The message encryption is implemented via symmetric encryption using Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), Galois Counter Mode (GCM) with 128-bit or 256-bit key size." · MLE enforcement levels are Mandatory, Optional, Not Applicable per API; Visa lets developers 'experiment with MLE in lower environments (Sandbox and Certification) before MLE is applied to the Production environment'. claim: VDP's JWE profile supports both symmetric (A256GCMKW with API key/shared secret) and asymmetric (RSA-OAEP-256) key wrapping, uses JOSE compact serialization, and suffixes '..' rather than '==' padding.
title: jwe-jws (JSON Web Encryption and Object Signing (JWE/JWS))
note: Quote: "Format: Values are AGCM256KW (Symmetric), RSA-OAEP-256 (Asymmetric)." · Page: 'Visa has chosen to suffix ".." to the Base64URL encoded values, instead of the more popular == convention.' claim: For most third-party agents, Visa's support relationship is mediated by a sponsoring issuer or acquirer that acts as liaison; only agents enrolling in non-sponsored products register directly with Visa.
title: Visa Partner | Third Party Agent Registration
note: Quote: "A Visa Client sponsor serves as a liaison between you and Visa" · 'The Visa product team overseeing the service you are enrolling in will assist you in determining if a Visa Client sponsor is required during onboarding.' Vendor claim on the same page: 'Visa provides support and resources to registered agents, including payments training, technical support, and marketing assistance'. · fetch curl

claim: Visa Acceptance Solutions publishes a response commitment of 1 to 2 business days for developer support requests submitted by form, with a masked phone number and peer channels on GitHub and Stack Overflow.
title: Contact us | Visa Acceptance Developer Portal
note: Quote: "Please allow 1-2 business days for us to respond." · Phone shown as 'Call us at #######' in text but the link is tel:1-800-530-9095. Form fields: name, email, Merchant ID (MID), API Feature (includes 'AI Assistant', 'Developer MCP SDK', 'Intelligent Commerce Connect'), programming language, issue summary, error message. Peer help: 'Or get help from the Visa Acceptance developer community' linking github.com/CyberSource and stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/cybersource. Production issues are redirected: 'For questions about processing transactions, enabling services in Production or unlocking your account, please contact Client Services.' Sandbox is self-serve: 'After completing the evaluation registration process, you will be able to send test transactions' but 'You should not perform load or stress testing in the sandbox'. · fetch curl

claim: Visa Acceptance's Support Center offers live chat and support-case submission, but both are behind sign-in; unauthenticated visitors get knowledge articles only.

note: Quote: "Sign in to view additional content, start a chat or submit a support case." · Portal covers 'our Visa Acceptance Solutions and Cybersource portfolios'. Sign-in routes to businesscenter.visaacceptance.com/ebc2/ or Visa SSO (sso.trusted.visa.com). Popular topics: Getting started, Reason/decline codes, Security keys, Reports, Refunds/voids, Business center access. · fetch curl

claim: Incident communication for Visa Acceptance Solutions is a public Atlassian Statuspage with email and SMS subscriptions, RSS/Atom feeds and an incident history; it lists the Developer Center and Support Center as monitored components.
title: Visa Acceptance Solutions Status
note: Quote: "We use this page to communicate service availability and status for Visa Acceptance Solutions. Subscribe to get real-time updates via Email, SMS." · 'All Systems Operational' at fetch. Components include API Connection/Endpoints (Flex, Rest API, Webhooks), 'Corporate and Support Web Sites' (Corporate Site, Developer Center, Status Page, Support Center), Payment Gateway Processing by processor (e.g., Chase Paymentech, Elavon, WorldPay), Visa Platform Connect gateways. Subscription terms reference 'the Atlassian Terms of Service'. A parallel page at https://status.cybersource.com/ ('Cybersource Status') remains live with the older component list (SCMP, Simple Order API, SOAP Toolkit). No equivalent status page exists for the Visa Developer Center. · fetch curl

claim: The Cybersource Developer Community (still linked as 'Support & Community' from the Visa Acceptance developer portal) had 64.5K members but only 513 Cybersource discussions versus 10,964 Authorize.net discussions, and its announcements block still carries 2011-era notices; the live host bot-walls automated fetches.
title: Home - Cybersource Developer Community
publisher: Cybersource Developer Community (Visa Inc.), Wayback Machine capture
note: Quote: "1,666 Solutions 10.9K Discussions 64.5K Members" · Archived 2026-05-14. 'Cybersource Developer Community 513 discussions Authorize.net Developer Community 10964 discussions'. Recent posts (May 2026) show '0 replies'. Stale announcement text: 'Authorize.Net will be exhibiting at the 2011 Mobile Commerce Forum, in Houston, TX, October 10th through 12th.' Live URL returned HTTP 403 'Just a moment...' (Cloudflare) to curl and WebFetch on 2026-09-25. The community is still Cybersource-branded although the portal that links to it is Visa Acceptance-branded. · fetch curl

claim: The client portal formerly branded Visa Online is now defined in the Visa Rules as 'Visa Access', a password-protected site for Members, VisaNet Processors and other authorised users.
title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules
note: Quote: "A password-protected website that provides Members, VisaNet Processors, and other authorized users with access to Visa information, formerly known as Visa Online." · Glossary entry ID# 0025360, p.904 (Edition Apr 2026, Last Updated Apr 2025). https://www.visaonline.com/ redirects to a login page (secure.visaonline.com) titled 'Index' with no public description. Related gated self-service tools defined at ID# 0026479: 'Client Portfolio Management Self-Service Tools ... comprising the following: Program Request Management (PRM), Electronic Client Information Questionnaire (eCIQ), Visa Client Support Application (VCSA)'. The 'Client Service Provider Directory' is 'used for Member-to-Member communication and problem resolution' (ID# 0030656). Monthly account statements 'can be consulted in Visa Access' (ID# 0031178). · fetch curl

claim: Visa's operational communications to clients go by email to two mandated roles per Member, the Primary Center Manager and a Senior Officer, and include the weekly Visa Business News.
title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules
note: Quote: "Primary operational contact who receives all critical corporate and operational email communications from Visa that may be urgent or require a response" · Glossary ID# 0031041 (Primary Center Manager) and ID# 0031042: 'The Senior Officer receives the same email communications as the Primary Center Manager, including the weekly Visa Business News.' Rule 2.1.3.1 (ID# 0007725) requires Members to register these contacts 'in the My Organization’s Contacts module of the Client Directory via Visa Access' within 10 business days of a BID implementation or change. Visa Business News itself is gated. · fetch curl

claim: Visa's public merchant support page is a document library with no contact channel; merchants get a periodic digest of Visa Business News rather than direct access to it.
title: Merchant Resource Library | Visa
note: Quote: "The Visa Merchant Business News Digest provides a summary of recent Visa Business News publications that highlight key merchant-related publications." · Seed https://usa.visa.com/support/merchant.html redirects here. 'Updated periodically.' Library categories: Best Practices, Disputes, Security and Risk, EMV. No phone, email, form or hours on the page. WebFetch of the same page also found 'no direct merchant support contact information'. · fetch curl

claim: Visa University, Visa's client training arm, commits to a 1 to 2 business-day response on its contact form, which includes a 'BID inquiry' category for client institutions.

note: Quote: "A member of our support team will respond to your inquiry within 1-2 business days." · Form topics: Course question, Course enrollment, Account issue, BID inquiry, Not receiving emails, Payment/billing question, Digital Payments Library, certificate/certification programmes, Exams, Cancellation request. claim: Visa University runs exam-based professional certifications (Dispute Resolution, Payments Cybersecurity, Portfolio Management) with digital badges, alongside a seven-week Wharton co-branded certificate and a 1,200-video streaming library.

note: Quote: "Our certification programs consist of required exams with recommended courses that help you prepare to take the exams." · Homepage: 'Digital Payments Catalyst A seven-week certificate program pairing the academic excellence of Wharton faculty with the real-world expertise of Visa leaders' with 'Registration for our September 2026 program is now open'; 'Digital Payments Library ... featuring 1,200+ videos, 17 courses, 20+ playlists'. Course topics: Dispute Resolution, Fraud, Operations, Payments Cybersecurity, Payments Landscape, Portfolio Management. Pricing not checked. · fetch curl
